abstract: Enhancers direct precise gene expression patterns, but how syntax, the organization of transcription factor binding sites (TFBSs), shapes enhancer activity and tissue specificity remains unclear. Here we test 460,800 organizations of ETS and GATA TFBSs in Ciona embryos. All elements contain the same number, type and affinity of TFBSs, yet only 18% are active. Single TFBS orientation flips convert 54,000 inert elements into functional enhancers, establishing syntax as a critical determinant of enhancer activity and revealing strict syntax rules. We identify enhancer syntaxes in which activity depends on placement of differing-affinity TFBSs (dependent-syntax) and robust-syntaxes that are active regardless of TFBS affinity placement. We develop a Single-cell, whole-Embryo Massively Parallel Reporter Assay (SEMPRA), which shows that dependent-syntax is critical for maintaining sensitivity to the trans environment and tissue specificity, whereas robust-syntaxes yield broadly active enhancers. Our exhaustive enhancer rearrangement coupled with whole-embryo MPRA and SEMPRA reveals that enhancer syntax tunes responsiveness to the cellular environment, thereby encoding tissue specificity.
